title: Over 157M expected to shop in stores, online on Super Saturday

facts.fact: According to the NRF and Prosper Insights & Analytics survey, about 157.2 million people were expected to do holiday shopping in stores, online or both on the final Saturday before Christmas.
facts.quote: About 157.2 million people are expected to do holiday shopping in stores, online or both this weekend on the final Saturday before Christmas

facts.fact: The NRF/Prosper survey found 44% of respondents planned to shop both in-store and online on Super Saturday, up from 41% the prior year.
facts.quote: The survey found that 44% of those polled plan to shop both in-store and online, up from 41% last year.

facts.fact: The NRF/Prosper survey found 31% of respondents expected to shop exclusively in-store on Super Saturday, down from 37% the prior year.
facts.quote: About 31% expect to shop exclusively in-store, down from 37% last year

facts.fact: The NRF/Prosper survey found 24% of respondents planned to shop online only on Super Saturday, up from 22% the prior year.
facts.quote: while 24% plan to shop online only. That’s up from 22% last year.

facts.fact: The NRF reported that 141.9 million people shopped on the Super Saturday weekend the previous year.
facts.quote: That’s up from 141.9 million people last year.

facts.fact: The NRF and Prosper estimated 197 million people shopped between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday in 2024, down from 200.4 million the prior year.
facts.quote: The NRF and Prosper estimated that 197 million people shopped between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday. While that’s down from 200.4 million people last year

facts.fact: Shoppers reported they were likely to spend $902 on holiday shopping in 2024, of which $641 would be spent on gifts for family, friends or coworkers.
facts.quote: Shoppers reported they’re likely to spend $902 this year; of that amount, $641 will be spent on gifts for family, friends or coworkers.

facts.fact: Among those polled, 37% expected to visit department stores to finish shopping, 27% a discount store, and 25% a clothing and accessory store.
facts.quote: 37% will visit department stores, 27% will go to a discount store and 25% plan to patronize a clothing and accessory store.

facts.fact: Apparel or accessories were the top gift category purchased so far, with 50% of consumers buying in that category; toys were at 32% and gift cards at 26%.
facts.quote: Apparel or accessories comprise the top gifts people have bought so far, with 50% of consumers making a purchase in the category.

facts.fact: Among shoppers with at least half their shopping left, 37% said they were still figuring out what to buy and 27% cited other financial priorities before December.
facts.quote: Thirty-seven percent of people with at least half of their shopping left to do said they were still figuring out what to buy, while 27% reported having other financial priorities before December.

facts.fact: 71% of consumers are likely to shop the week after Christmas, according to an NRF and Prosper survey.
facts.quote: Most consumers — 71% — are also likely to shop the week after Christmas too.

facts.fact: Nearly half of survey respondents said they want to take advantage of holiday sales and promotions the week after Christmas.
facts.quote: Nearly half of respondents said they want to take advantage of holiday sales and promotions that week

facts.fact: 26% of survey respondents said they want to use gift cards the week after Christmas.
facts.quote: while 26% said they want to use gift cards.

facts.fact: 16% of survey respondents said they will exchange or return unwanted gifts or holiday items.
facts.quote: Sixteen percent said they’ll exchange or return unwanted gifts or holiday items.

facts.fact: The NRF and Prosper survey obtained its data from 7,861 adults.
facts.quote: The NRF and Prosper obtained their data by surveying 7,861 adults from Dec. 2 through Dec. 9.

facts.fact: Per a CNBC headline linked on the page, consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected.
facts.quote: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected, complicating Fed’s inflation fight

facts.fact: Per a YouGov report announced in a company press release, just 35% of measured U.S. brands are bipartisan.
facts.quote: Just 35% of measured U.S. brands are bipartisan, YouGov report finds From YouGov November 03, 2026
